text:
marta: heads-up - spike in kms:Decrypt from backup-restore-worker in prod-eu-west-1 at ~04:06 UTC. Not normal volume.

encops-bot: :warning: ALERT KMS_ANOMALY - key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/ff11ee22 increased decrypt rate 8x. alert id KMS-20260323-99

devin: which service/instance group?

marta: backup-restore-worker-{prod,replica}-3, lots of repeated Decrypts and a few CreateGrant entries. CloudTrail sample: 

```
2026-03-23T04:06:10Z kms:Decrypt userIdentity:AssumedRole:backup-restore-worker
Resource: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/ff11ee22
RequestParameters: {ciphertextBlob: REDACTED}
```

priya: I pushed an RBAC cleanup last week but targeted only the CI roles. Did anyone touch the uploader/restore role mapping?

theo: I rolled a small restore optimization (PR #5012) that switched to synchronous decrypts and removed a short-lived in-process plaintext cache. That was to avoid sensitive data lingering in memory. Could be related.

marta: removal of caching + a retry loop on failure = repeated decrypt attempts. Check stack traces for retry/backoff.

priya: listing grants on the key now. CLI I used: 

```
aws kms list-grants --key-id ff11ee22 --query 'Grants[*].{grantee:GranteePrincipal,iss:IssuingAccountId,created:CreationDate}'
```

priya: found multiple active grants issued to arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/backup-restore-worker, creation times cluster at 04:05-04:07.

devin: can we revoke those grants selectively? We can call aws kms retire-grant / revoke-grant but need the grantId.

ops-runner: temporary mitigation: slowing down restore workers via k8s HPA scale-down and patching client to fail-fast. Doing now.

marta: please don't revoke the CMK key policy. That will block legitimate restores. We need minimal blast radius. Options: 1) revoke STS sessions for the restore role, 2) retire grants created during the window, 3) throttle restore queue.

theo: I'll cut a hotfix to reintroduce a short-lived prefix cache that stores plaintext for the restore session and add a jittered exponential backoff to decrypt retries. PR incoming.

priya: I pulled CloudTrail for iam:CreatePolicy / kms:CreateGrant around the time window and forwarded to splunk index(encops). Splunk query: 

```
index=encops eventName=CreateGrant OR eventName=Decrypt | stats count by eventName, userIdentity.arn
```

priya: results show a burst of CreateGrant from the restore role, not from human operators. Could be the worker creating ephemeral grants for each object and then retrying quickly on transient IO errors.

devin: action plan:
- ops-runner: keep restores throttled until grant activity stabilizes.
- priya: retire the grants created 04:05-04:10 and keep grant audit feed on.
- theo: deploy hotfix (cache + backoff) to prod-restore workers, target deploy in 15m.
- marta: create incident channel and escalate if traffic doesn't drop in 10m.

encops-bot: ACTION: created incident channel #incident-kms-2798812345 id INC-20260323-42

ops-runner: scaled down HPA and applied k8s patch to limit concurrent restores to 4 per pod. Decrypt volume dropped ~70% within 3 minutes.

priya: retired 14 grants issued during the window with aws kms retire-grant --grant-id <id>. Logged each retire call to splunk.

marta: nice. Also we should consider a longer-term policy change: forbid automatic CreateGrant calls from worker roles and instead centralize grant issuance via an auditored helper service that returns temporary tokens. Thoughts?

devin: agreed. Centralizing reduces grant proliferation and gives better observability. We can also add a quota on grants-per-role-per-minute enforced via a lambda watcher.

theo: hotfix deployed and validated in canary. Reinstated a 20s in-memory plaintext cache scoped to the restore job lifetime, with strict memzero and immediate eviction on completion. Also added backoff for Decrypt errors: base 200ms jittered, max 5s.

marta: excellent. Follow-ups: postmortem to answer root cause (agent change removed cache), update the RBAC playbook to include grant rate limits, add grant-creation alert runbook, and audit the codebase for other places we removed ephemeral caches without compensating controls.

priya: I'll own postmortem and schedule a blameless review.

devin: assign remediation ticket to infra/security for grant centralization and add E2E test to prevent future cache removal without compensating telemetry.

marta: thanks team. Closing thread when incident channel notes are posted.

(ends)
